paragraphs: Friend, here's what Paul is really after in this letter. He tells Timothy, "The goal of our instruction is the love that comes from a pure heart, a clear conscience, and a sincere faith." (1 Timothy 1:5) Love is the point. Teaching that doesn't aim there has wandered off the road.

Now look at the folks Paul warns about. They "want to be teachers of the law, but they do not understand what they are saying or that which they so confidently assert." (1 Timothy 1:7) Confidence is not the same as understanding, friend, and I have been loud and wrong in my own kitchen more than once. So Paul gives us a test: sound teaching "agrees with the glorious gospel of the blessed God." (1 Timothy 1:10-11)

So what do you do with that, baker? Keep your eyes on the gospel, and let what you learn lead you toward love instead of just a head full of speculation. Paul says the law is good "if one uses it legitimately." (1 Timothy 1:8) That's the kind of baking I want to do, using God's Word the way it was meant to be used, with a pure heart and a sincere faith.
